title: Varying band size and which instrument they miss
summary: The band can shrink to four or six pieces or drop an instrument; Zanco misses banjo and trombone most. Conner mentions Buddy Bolden's two clarinets.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Do you ever work with, uh, any, uh, any less than the, uh, seven or six or seven instruments that you mentioned?

Sometimes, yeah. Well, uh, you take some of these, uh, patio parties we might play. They might want more of a, you know, a quiet and down music. So we, uh, we'll mute the trumpet, use a clarinet, piano, drums. Sometimes we'll operate with four pieces, sometimes five, sometimes six, sometimes a full eight. You know, it depends on the type of music that, uh, particular people will want at their party, you see. I mean, uh, I've seen times, uh, where we sound just a few pieces. We have, we sound as loud as the Eureka Brass Band. And I've also seen times where we sound like something that should have been in the blue room. We can hold it down there quiet at times, you see.
Do you ever play without bass or without piano or without drums or without this or without that?

Well, let's see. We've, uh, we've played without a piano already. We've played without drums already. We've played without bass already. Matter of fact, we even play without cornet already. You, you got a bunch of guys that just want to play and they know what they're doing. I mean, you could take a, a flute and a banjo and they could give a concert if both of them know what they're doing. You know, they could, they could, uh, be as effective as if they had a, maybe a six or seven piece band there.
Which instrument do you miss the most when you don't have it?

Uh, I would think maybe the... Stay out of the rhythm section. I would think the drum. I don't know. I mean, some, you know, maybe other people might have a different opinion of that, but I think the drum. A lot of times, I mean, uh, the drum, the, uh, bass will take the place of the drum. Or the banjo will take the place of the drum, you see. And I've just gotten so that, uh, I don't know if I could really play anymore without listening to a banjo sitting alongside of it. I've played already without a banjo and I just got into that, into that rut. I have to be listening to a banjo playing, see. The same thing with a trombone. I have to be listening to a trombone. Actually, by having those other instruments like that, they're helping me keep my timing, you know.
Yeah, well, that banjo sure gives you chords and everything. Helps you along. All that. I thought of another band that used to have two clarinets, Buddy Bolden. You've seen the picture of that?
Oh. With two clarinets? I'll show it to you.
Willie Warner. I'll show you that picture sometime. Yeah, that's an old tradition, you know. Get some good stuff that way. I'm just about to run out. How about you?
